name: Claude Fable 5.2

setting.label: High · adaptive thinking
setting.note: Adaptive thinking is always on. High is the Claude API default. Try xhigh on a representative task before raising effort for a long run.

description: Anthropic’s premium model for open-ended engineering and demanding reasoning. Its standard input and output rates are twice those of Claude Opus 5.5, with the same cache-read rate.

price.note: Standard first-party Claude API rates apply across the full context window. Cache writes, Fast mode, data residency, and server tools can change the bill. Output includes billed thinking tokens.

coding.bestFor: Planning complex migrations or resolving conflicting requirements across a codebase.
coding.example: Map how several services share a data schema, then propose a staged migration with compatibility tests.
coding.limitation: Run the project’s tests and review the changes. Longer reasoning and tool loops can raise total cost.
coding.stepUp: Start with Opus 5.5 for well-scoped work. Try Fable when the change crosses several systems or an initial plan leaves gaps.

debugging.bestFor: Investigating difficult failures with several plausible causes.
debugging.example: Compare test logs and recent dependency changes to explain an intermittent failure in a data export.
debugging.limitation: Logs can support multiple explanations. Reproduce the suspected cause before changing production code.
debugging.stepUp: Use Fable for a second pass when an initial investigation cannot distinguish between explanations.

analysis.bestFor: Reconciling complex evidence across long reports, charts, and spreadsheets.
analysis.example: Trace conflicting renewal totals back to the definitions used in each report.
analysis.limitation: Verify calculated totals against the spreadsheet and ask for the source of each disputed value.
analysis.stepUp: Use Opus 5.5 for a single dataset. Try Fable when several sources use incompatible definitions.

research.bestFor: Synthesizing large sets of sources when the evidence conflicts.
research.example: Compare migration requirements across vendor guides and build a decision log linked to the original documents.
research.limitation: Open the cited documents to verify claims, dates, and compatibility requirements.
research.stepUp: Start with Opus 5.5, then use Fable to revisit unresolved tradeoffs.

name: Claude Opus 5.5

setting.label: Medium · adaptive thinking
setting.note: Adaptive thinking is always on. Medium is the Claude API default. Try high for long or ambiguous work if a representative evaluation shows a gain.

description: Anthropic’s general-purpose model for substantial coding and knowledge work. It offers the same context and output limits as Claude Fable 5.2 at half the standard input and output rates.

price.note: Standard first-party Claude API rates apply across the full context window. Cache writes, Fast mode, data residency, and server tools can change the bill. Output includes billed thinking tokens.

coding.bestFor: Implementing code changes with clear acceptance criteria.
coding.example: Refactor a PowerShell reporting script, preserve its output format, and add regression tests.
coding.limitation: Check the diff and run the acceptance tests in the intended environment.
coding.stepUp: Try Fable 5.2 when a change spans several systems or the acceptance criteria conflict.

debugging.bestFor: Tracing failures across logs, configuration, and recent code changes.
debugging.example: Find which change made a scheduled report fail and propose a minimal fix.
debugging.limitation: Confirm the failure and fix with a reproducible test.
debugging.stepUp: Try Fable 5.2 if competing explanations survive your first set of checks.

analysis.bestFor: Explaining trends and checking formulas across structured data.
analysis.example: Reconcile totals across two monthly exports and list which rows account for the difference.
analysis.limitation: Recalculate results in the worksheet before sharing them.
analysis.stepUp: Try Fable 5.2 when multiple sources use conflicting definitions.

research.bestFor: Comparing documented options and drafting a practical recommendation.
research.example: Summarize three vendor migration guides and list their prerequisites with source links.
research.limitation: Verify eligibility, service limits, and dates against the original documentation.
research.stepUp: Try Fable 5.2 when evidence is inconsistent or depends on interacting constraints.

writing.bestFor: Turning technical notes into a clear customer-facing document.
writing.example: Draft a migration handover with the agreed scope, dependencies, and sign-off criteria.
writing.limitation: Check each commitment against the signed scope and the current plan.
writing.stepUp: Use a larger effort budget when the source documents conflict or leave gaps.

presentations.bestFor: Structuring a decision deck from technical evidence.
presentations.example: Create an outline comparing three hosting options with assumptions, tradeoffs, and a decision slide.
presentations.limitation: Verify figures and source claims before laying out the slides.
presentations.stepUp: Try Fable 5.2 for comparing alternatives with several conflicting constraints.
